channel.title: Wire — tech digest
channel.description: One digest a day, merged from thirty sources.

item.title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus
item.description: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Is AI ruining my brain?
item.description: Has using AI at work made me worse at other things in my life? (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Stop Thinking of LLMs as Next-Token Predictors
item.description: “Next-token predictor” is the wrong mental model for LLMs (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Google Mantis: An Agentic Vulnerability Scanning Harness for Reducing False Positives
item.description: Google has open-sourced Mantis, an AI-agent framework designed to automate the software vulnerability lifecycle, from identifying and validating vulnerabilities to reproducing and fixing them. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: How Figma Uses AI Agents for Security
item.description: The engineering team at software company Figma recently documented how they built AI agents to help their security team investigate alerts, search past incidents, check company systems, and even prepare code fixes. (1 source: infoq)

item.description: I recommend reading the whole thread, but I linked to the part I found the most relevant. I believe the same is true for programming. Comments (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Surviving Code Reviews in the era of AI
item.description: My coworkers are all fully AI pilled. As a consequence, every PR that comes my way for review is on average ~6k lines of diff. (1 source: lobsters)
